# LovelyCarve integration

Source: lamco-admin/lamfold `crates/lamfold-udf` 0.1.1, revision
`fabaad6af0c28b80535307b339b84110f3a3c12e`.
https://github.com/lamco-admin/lamfold/tree/fabaad6af0c28b80535307b339b84110f3a3c12e/crates/lamfold-udf

MIT OR Apache-2.0; original attribution and licenses retained. The host's
UDF-specific changes are distributed under these same licenses. This is a
pure Rust, read-only library over the existing vendored lamfold BlockSource.

The upstream frontend was split into descriptor, inode and volume modules and
hardened: tag version/checksum/location/CRC coverage; bounded primary/backup
anchor and main/reserve VDS selection; explicit single physical Type-1 map;
all partition references and allocated ranges checked; 512–4096-byte blocks;
FE/EFE and AED continuation chains; exact logical reads and sparse semantics;
bounded inode/cache/directory/chain storage; strict Unicode/FID parsing;
hard-link identity; unfollowed decoded symlinks; role-specific timestamps with
known UTC offset only. Unsupported maps/streams/strategies fail explicitly.
No C, FFI, system mount or extraction dependency is used.

Positive fixtures: upstream udf102.img and udf201.img, losslessly zlib
compressed here, generated by mkudffs and populated by the Linux UDF driver.
The upstream 2.01 generation script is retained. Invented fixtures and their
Python generator are CC0-1.0. See tests/fixtures/manifest.json for hashes and
../../../docs/formats/UDF.md for supported scope, limits and validation.
